title: Protestors in Amsterdam storm Microsoft AI Data Center construction site
gist: About a hundred protesters overran a Microsoft AI data center construction site in Amsterdam owned by Pure Data Centers, the start of a 'Stop Dirty Data Centers' coalition campaign across 16 countries and 85 European locations on Nov 6-7, 2026, demanding an immediate moratorium on large data centers in Europe. Forum repost of Reuters/Tom's Hardware reporting.

insights.claim: About a hundred protesters overran a Microsoft data center under construction in Amsterdam, owned by Pure Data Centers.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Physical disruption of construction sites raises execution and timeline risk for hyperscaler AI capacity build-outs in Europe.
insights.quote: A Microsoft data center under construction in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, has been overrun by about a hundred protesters
insights.locator: A Microsoft data center under construction

insights.claim: The 'Stop Dirty Data Centers' coalition planned actions across 16 countries on November 6-7, 2026, including Amsterdam, Dublin, Warsaw and another Microsoft site in Denmark, with a map showing 85 locations across Europe.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Coordinated, multi-country opposition signals organized social license risk for European data center siting rather than isolated NIMBYism.
insights.quote: A map on the site shows actions planned at 85 locations across Europe over the coming days.

insights.claim: The coalition is calling for an immediate moratorium on large data centers in Europe and aims to hold elected officials to account.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A political push for moratoria could constrain permitting and power allocation for AI data centers, favoring capacity in other regions and existing sites.
insights.quote: We’re calling for an immediate moratorium on large data centres in Europe!

insights.claim: Microsoft said it respects the right to peaceful expression but does not condone unlawful action, while Pure Data Centers asked protesters to leave and engage in dialogue.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Corporate responses remain conciliatory, suggesting operators expect to negotiate with communities rather than face immediate project halts.
insights.quote: We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue
